item.title: Humaiun: Bangladesh reaffirms commitment to multilateralism, UN reform
item.description:
Bangladesh remains firmly committed to multilateralism and supports meaningful UN reform to address global challenges State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said in a message marking United Nations Day, on Saturday.
He said the government, under Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s leadership, remained determined to strengthen democratic governance, uphold human rights and the rule of law, and promote accountable institutions.
The election of Bangladesh’s foreign minister as president of the 81st UN General Assembly underscored the government’s renewed impetus for multilateral engagement, he said.
Kobir said Bangladesh supported a more representative, transparent and effective UN, including meaningful reform of the Security Council, so that the organization could respond to contemporary realities and deliver for all.
“At a time of growing geopolitical tensions, armed conflicts, humanitarian crises and widening inequalities, multilateralism is not merely an option, it is an imperative,” he said.
He called for renewed commitment to dialogue, peaceful settlement of disputes, sovereign equality and respect for international law.
Highlighting Bangladesh’s contribution to global peace, the state minister said the country’s engagement with the UN was rooted in action and solidarity.
As one of the leading contributors to UN peacekeeping operations, Bangladesh’s peacekeepers continued to serve in challenging environments worldwide, he said.
He reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to advancing women’s participation in peacekeeping and decision-making on peace and security.
Kobir said Bangladesh’s partnership with the UN extended to sustainable development, disaster resilience, poverty reduction, gender equality and humanitarian action.
Noting that Bangladesh continued to host more than 1.2 million Rohingyas forcibly displaced from Myanmar, he called for sustained international support for their early and sustainable return to Myanmar.
He also stressed the need to ensure finance, technology and capacity-building support for developing countries, least developed countries and climate-vulnerable nations as the international community pursued the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
Extending warm greetings to the UN and its member states, Kobir said United Nations Day highlighted the enduring relevance of the UN Charter and collective action in addressing shared global challenges.
“Let us work together to restore trust, bridge divisions and build a world where peace, justice and prosperity are shared by all,” he said.

item.title: Dengue: 6 more die, 1,898 hospitalized in 24 hrs
item.description:
Six more people died of dengue and 1,898 new patients were hospitalized across the country in 24 hours until 8:00am on Saturday.
With the latest fatalities, the dengue death toll has risen to 376 in the country this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Among the deaths, two were reported in Chittagong division and one each in Dhaka South City Corporation, Khulna and Rajshahi divisions, it said.
Since January 1 this year, a total of 121,699 dengue patients were admitted to hospitals across the country. Of them, 115,132 have recovered.

item.title: IGP: Police may initiate extortion cases on digital evidence alone
item.description:
Police will be empowered to file cases against extortionists on their own initiative, without requiring public complaints, under a proposed new law, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir has said.
The proposed law will allow police to take action against suspected extortionists based on digital evidence or information from other sources, he said.
“Extortionists are either criminals or connected to people in positions of power. As a result, people are often afraid to testify against them or lodge complaints with police,” the IGP said.
He made the remarks while responding to questions from journalists after a community policing meeting at Khulna Metropolitan Police Lines on Saturday afternoon.
Fakir said he had proposed to the home minister that a new law be enacted to strengthen action against extortion.
“Under the proposed law, police will be able to file cases and take action on their own initiative without requiring complaints from the public. If evidence, including digital evidence, is found, appropriate action can be taken against the accused. You will see a new law being introduced in the coming days,” he said.
The IGP said the initiative was aimed at eliminating extortion from society.
On rebuilding public trust in police, Fakir acknowledged that the force had become distanced from the public due to its activities over the past 17 years. He said his visit to Khulna was aimed at restoring public confidence and working to establish peace.
“Joint operations are underway against drugs, juvenile gangs, criminals and extortionists,” he said, adding that a legal framework was being developed with approval from the ministries of home affairs and finance to make police operations more effective.
He also said community policing would operate as a dedicated branch of the police force.
On the law and order situation in Khulna, the IGP said violence involving criminals had created fear among the public, with some criminals being killed and others committing murders.
“When police enforce the law, some demand the use of force. If force is used, they call the police fascist; if it is not used, they call the police weak. We do not want this,” he said.
He called for collective efforts to establish peace and justice and eliminate corruption through an effective police force.
Asked about the deterioration of law and order, Fakir recalled the situation after August 5, 2024, saying police had been absent from many areas and criminal activities had been widespread.
“Police have now regained their morale and resumed operations across the country. Not every problem can be resolved overnight, but the situation has improved,” he said.
The IGP said police wanted to become more humane and public-friendly, although some people argued that criminals no longer feared law enforcers.
He noted that some offenders resumed criminal activities shortly after being brought to justice, adding that police were developing policies to prevent repeat offences.
Fakir also said drugs had become entrenched in society over the past 17 years and that the current government had adopted a zero-tolerance policy towards narcotics.

item.title: Russia, Ukraine agree to US-brokered, 1 city ceasefire
item.description:
US first lady Melania Trump helped broker a ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia in the city of Oleshky, the White House announced Friday. The localized truce, according to the White House, is slated to begin on October 29.
The Ukrainian city occupied by Russia on the frontline of the war faces a humanitarian crisis and only around 2,000 people still live there. Prior to the war, the city had a population of around 24,000.
Oleshky has been under blockade since 2025 and was first occupied when Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.
The city is located in southern Ukraine, just 9 kilometers (around 5.6 miles) from the major city of Kherson.
“Oleshky’s remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water,” Melania Trump said in a statement. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks.”
Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, thanked the first lady for securing the deal.
“Under our agreement: first a ceasefire will be put in place; second, humanitarian aid will be delivered to Oleshky; and third, civilians will be allowed to move freely out of Oleshky,” Lubinets said in a video message posted on Telegram. “The operation will be carried out gradually and is extremely challenging to implement.”
Russia also confirmed the agreement and said it will halt fire earlier than what the White House announced at 0400 local time (0100 GMT) on October 27.
According to the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe Office for Democratic Institutions and Human Rights, residents in Oleshky say Russian occupying forces prevented them from leaving the city. Oleshky residents also say Russia has used civilians to shield military positions in the city — a war crime under international humanitarian law.
The ceasefire deal in Oleshky comes as US, Ukrainian and Russian negotiators are expected to meet in Abu Dhabi next month to discuss ending the war.
“The plan is to meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course,” Zelensky told the US conservative Hudson Institute think tank.
In comments to Russian state news outlet TASS, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov also said preparations are underway for a three-way meeting in mid-November. Russian President Vladimir Putin said security would be a main topic for the Abu Dhabi talks.
“That is the security of both countries, Russia and Ukraine, after there has been a transition to a peace settlement,” Peskov said.
The Kremlin spokesperson said Russia only sees the Europeans at the table during a later stage in the talks. European leaders such as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz have said Europe must be involved in future Ukraine peace talks.
“It is clear that the architecture of European security cannot be discussed without other participants,” Peskov added.
US President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated at Zelensky, and is pressuring him to “make a deal.”
Trump has blamed Ukraine for rising diesel prices in the US, as the US-Israeli war against Iran has caused the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and drove up the cost of gas at the pump for American consumers.
Trump has backed a deal to buy diesel from Russia to lower prices at fuel pumps, drawing criticism from Ukraine. The Kremlin said Friday that the first tanker of Russian diesel has set sail for the US despite the backlash from Ukraine.
Most recently, there has been controversy that tech billionaire Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of the Starshield military communications system that Ukraine relies on, possibly with the backing of Trump.
Trump has denied that he ordered restrictions on Starlink. He also defended Musk in comments to reporters on Friday and said, “Elon will never do anything wrong.”
“You know, whether I called or whether somebody else called, doesn’t make any difference,” Trump said. “I guess the bottom line, he put it back.”
Meanwhile, Zelensky and Ukraine said Friday that the system was still being throttled in Ukraine.
“It works, but it’s still limited,” Zelensky told US broadcaster ABC News.
A source in Ukraine’s Defense Ministry told AFP news agency and other news outlets that Ukrainians were witnessing “instances of signal loss” when using Starshield.
“There is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted,” the source added.

item.title: ধ্বংসের মুখে আমাজন, উধাও ২৪ কোটি একরের বনাঞ্চল
item.description:
পৃথিবীর প্রাকৃতিক জলবায়ু নিয়ন্ত্রণ ও বৃষ্টিপাত চক্র বজায় রাখার ক্ষেত্রে আমাজন বনের গুরুত্ব অপরিসীম। আমাজন কনজারভেশনের মনিটরিং অব দ্য আন্দিজ আমাজন প্রোগ্রামের (এমএএপি) এক প্রতিবেদনে বলা হয়েছে, আমাজনের প্রাথমিক বনাঞ্চলের ২৪ কোটি একর জমি ধ্বংস হয়ে গেছে, যা যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের টেক্সাস ও ক্যালিফোর্নিয়া অঙ্গরাজ্যের মোট আয়তনের সমান।

আমাজন কনজারভেশনের মনিটরিং অব দ্য আন্দিজ আমাজন প্রোগ্রামের তথ্যমতে, আমাজন অববাহিকার ৯টি দেশ জুড়ে থাকা মোট প্রাথমিক বনাঞ্চলের প্রায় ১৫ শতাংশ ইতিমধ্যে চিরতরে হারিয়ে গেছে। মানুষের জমি দখলের তীব্র প্রবণতা এবং দাবানলের ধ্বংসযজ্ঞ এই হ্রাসের প্রধান কারণ। ২০২১ সালের প্রতিবেদনে আমাজন বনাঞ্চল হ্রাসের হার ১৩ দশমিক ২ শতাংশ বলা হয়েছিল। কাগজে–কলমে ব্যবধান সামান্য মনে হলেও বাস্তবে এটি এক বিশাল এলাকাজুড়ে পরিবেশ বিপর্যয় ঘটিয়েছে। আমাজন বন ধ্বংসের ৭৯ দশমিক ৪ শতাংশই ঘটেছে ব্রাজিলে। এরপর বলিভিয়ায় ৬ দশমিক ২ শতাংশ, পেরুতে ৫ দশমিক ৮ শতাংশ এবং কলম্বিয়ায় ৪ দশমিক ৫ শতাংশ ধ্বংস হয়েছে।

প্রতিবেদনে দেখা গেছে, ২০২২ থেকে ২০২৫ সালের মধ্যবর্তী সময়ে আরও ৩ কোটি ২২ লক্ষ একর বনাঞ্চল ধ্বংস হয়েছে। এই হার ইয়েলোস্টোন ন্যাশনাল পার্কের আয়তনের চেয়ে প্রায় ১৫ গুণ বেশি। ২০২৩ সালের শক্তিশালী এল নিনোর প্রভাবে ২০২৪ সালে রেকর্ড পরিমাণ বনভূমি দাবানলে ভস্মীভূত হয়। জলবায়ু পরিবর্তনের পাশাপাশি আমাজনের ২৫ শতাংশ বন ধ্বংস হলে পুরো অববাহিকা স্থায়ীভাবে বদলে যাবে। আমাজনের বিশাল সব গাছ মাটি থেকে পানি টেনে নিয়ে বাষ্প আকারে বায়ুমণ্ডলে ছেড়ে দেয়। বাতাস এই জলীয় বাষ্পকে মহাদেশজুড়ে ছড়িয়ে দেয়, যাকে বিজ্ঞানীরা উড়ন্ত নদী বলেন। আমাজন তার নিজের বৃষ্টিপাতের প্রায় অর্ধেক নিজ থেকেই তৈরি করে। পানির এই প্রবাহ কয়েকবার ব্যবহৃত হয়।

গবেষক ম্যাট ফিনার জানিয়েছেন, সংবাদমাধ্যমের প্রতিবেদনে প্রায়ই বলা হয় আমাজন এক বিপজ্জনক মোড়ের কাছাকাছি পৌঁছাচ্ছে। প্রকৃত তথ্য হচ্ছে বনাঞ্চল উচ্ছেদ ও দাবানলে আমাজনের ১৫ শতাংশ ধ্বংস হয়ে গেছে। এর মাধ্যমে রেইনফরেস্ট টিকিয়ে রাখা জলবিজ্ঞান চক্রটি চিরতরে ব্যাহত হতে পারে। এই অঞ্চলের যে অংশ আগে থেকেই ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত হয়েছে, সেখানে প্রভাব সবচেয়ে দ্রুত পড়বে। পেরু ও বলিভিয়ার যেসব কৃষক ও সাধারণ মানুষ বৃষ্টির ওপর নির্ভরশীল, তাদের সামনে এখন বড় প্রশ্ন তৈরি হয়েছে। দূরবর্তী কোনো পরিবেশ সংকটের চেয়ে আকাশে বৃষ্টিবাহী মেঘ আসার অনিশ্চয়তাই তাদের জন্য এখন সবচেয়ে বড় বাস্তবতা।
